verses.text: Then I saw another mighty angel coming down from heaven, wrapped in a cloud, with a rainbow above his head. His face was like the sun, and his legs were like pillars of fire.
He held in his hand a small scroll, which lay open. He placed his right foot on the sea and his left foot on the land.
Then he cried out in a loud voice like the roar of a lion. And when he cried out, the seven thunders sounded their voices.
When the seven thunders had spoken, I was about to put it in writing. But I heard a voice from heaven saying, "Seal up what the seven thunders have said, and do not write it down."
Then the angel I had seen standing on the sea and on the land lifted up his right hand to heaven.
And he swore by Him who lives forever and ever, who created heaven and everything in it, the earth and everything in it, and the sea and everything in it: "There will be no more delay!
But in the days of the voice of the seventh angel, when he is about to sound his trumpet, the mystery of God will be fulfilled, just as He proclaimed to His servants the prophets."
Then the voice that I had heard from heaven spoke to me again, saying, "Go, take the small scroll that lies open in the hand of the angel standing on the sea and on the land."
And I went to the angel and said, "Give me the small scroll." "Take it and eat it," he said. "It will make your stomach bitter, but in your mouth it will be as sweet as honey."
So I took the small scroll from the angel's hand and ate it; and it was as sweet as honey in my mouth, but when I had eaten it, my stomach turned bitter.
And they told me, "You must prophesy again about many peoples and nations and tongues and kings."

context.author: John, who was on the island of Patmos (1:1, 4, 9); traditionally the apostle John
context.genre: Apocalypse, prophecy, and letter, full of symbols and visions
context.audience: Seven churches in the Roman province of Asia
context.setting: A mighty angel wrapped in a cloud, with a rainbow over his head and a face like the sun, stands with one foot on the sea and one on the land, holding a little scroll. Seven thunders speak, but John is told not to write them. The angel swears there will be no more delay, and John is told to eat the scroll, which is sweet in the mouth and bitter in the stomach.
context.custom: Eating a scroll is a prophet’s act of taking a message into himself. The raised hand is the gesture of an oath. “mystery of God” (v.7) is a secret plan now to be completed.
context.timelineImmediate: Chapter 11 shows the measuring of the temple and the two witnesses.
context.timelineBible: The scroll recalls Ezekiel 2:8–3:3, where Ezekiel eats a scroll sweet as honey. The oath uses language from Daniel 12:7. “Prophesy again” (v.11) recalls Jeremiah 1:10.

otBackground.note: The man in linen swears by him who lives forever.

overview.summary: A mighty angel gives John a little scroll to eat. It is sweet and bitter, and John must prophesy again to the nations.
overview.settingLine: An angel stands on sea and land.

history.t: Ezekiel and Jeremiah also received a message by eating or touching.
The giant statue astride a harbor may be echoed by the angel’s stance.

customs.t: A symbol for the sweetness of God’s word.

archaeology.t: Papyrus scrolls from the Roman world.
Writing in John’s day was on scrolls of papyrus or parchment. The little scroll John eats (10:9-10) recalls the scroll Ezekiel ate (Ezekiel 3:1-3).

overview.discussion: God’s word was sweet to John’s taste and bitter in his stomach. Have I found God’s word both sweet and hard to digest?
overview.book: The book of Revelation · 22 chapters. A vision of Christ, judgment, and the new creation, written to encourage persecuted believers.
overview.author: John
